title: Denmark – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Totalrådgiveraftale vedrørende rådgivning og bistand i forbindelse med restaurering af livgardens kaserne
description: Etablissement- og Terrænkommandoen udbyder en totalrådgiverkontrakt vedrørende totalrestaurering og opgradering af Livgardens Kasernes Bygning 1. Udbuddet gennemføres som udbud med forhandling, jf. udbudslovens § 61. Opgaven omhandler en totalrestaurering og opgradering af Livgardens Kasernes eksisterende bygning beliggende på Gothersgade 100, 1123 København K. Bygningen består af tre hovedelementer: en hovedbygning bestående af to fløje og tre pavilloner, en længebygning inkl. delvis kælder samt en staldbygning. Hertil kommer en selvstændig kælderetage i tilknytning til og med adgang fra staldbygningen. Alle førnævnte bygningselementer betegnes samlet som ”Bygning 1”. Opgaven vedrørende totalrestaurering og opgradering omfatter hele Bygning 1, dog med undtagelse af den selvstændige kælderetage samt dele af stueetagen i Længen. Bygherren har forud for udbuddet af totalrådgivningen foretaget en række forundersøgelser og udarbejdet et byggeprogram med tilhørende funktions- og rumprogram samt øvrige bilag, der beskriver intentionerne med og kravene til projektet. Af byggeprogrammet og de tilhørende bilag fremgår den bygningshistoriske redegørelse og værdisætning, som restaureringen skal følge, samt et bearbejdet idéoplæg og en disponering, som opgraderingen forventes at følge. Opgaven består herefter i at færdigudvikle og projektere nedrivnings-, restaurerings- og opgraderingsprojektet, udbyde arbejderne i entrepriser efter nærmere aftale med Bygherren samt varetage byggeledelsen og føre fagtilsyn under gennemførelsen af alle entreprisearbejder frem til den endelige idriftsættelse af den færdige bygning. Opgaven gennemføres i tæt samarbejde med Bygherren, dennes Bygherrerådgiver, repræsentanter for kasernens brugere, relevante fredningsmyndigheder samt entreprenøren på de enkelte entrepriser.

title: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE - RECAPITALIZE ANTI ARMOUR RANGE (MDB)
description: Advance Procurement Notice Recapitalize Anti Armour Range (MODIFIED DESIGN-BUILD) 5 CDSB Gagetown, Oromocto, NB. (with Security Requirements) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform design-builders of an upcoming contract opportunity at 5 CDSB Gagetown, Oromocto, NB. The purpose of this APN is to allow design-builders to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested design-builders to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Description of the Project and Services It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. Contract Number: HQ04022_86689 Title: Recapitalize Anti Armour Range Approximate Estimate: $109M Anticipated Posting: November 2026 Description: The proposed recapitalization work includes: Upgrade Firing Point 6 (FP6) to serve as a replacement for Firing Point 4 (FP4), ensuring continued Level 5/6 training capability during construction. The FP6 recapitalization includes four new 2 km long firing lanes, crossing lanes for target access, protective berms, fire base pads, unexploded ordnance (UXO) clearance, vegetation management, arc markers, buried electrical conduits for target systems, a multi-storey control tower, and a climate-controlled sentry shack. Once FP6 is operational, FP4 will be upgraded with four recapitalized firing lanes, crossing lanes, protective berms, tank table positions, UXO clearance, vegetation management, arc markers, buried electrical conduits New approximately 455 m² climate-controlled administrative building, and refurbishment of the existing control tower. Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing design-builders early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, design-builders that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, design-builders are asked to quote the following information, among other things:   Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number (Project number on the MERX notice); Contract number 86689 CN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored for. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the design-builders to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a design-builder:   has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation (Contract number listed on their request for sponsorship) being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package, and has submitted a proposal or a bid DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). title: Silmänpohjakuvaukset Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialueen diabeetikoille
description: Silmänpohjakuvaukset Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialueen diabeetikoille Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialue hankkii diabeettisen retinopatian seulontaan tarkoitetun silmänpohjakuvauspalvelun diabetesta sairastaville asiakkailleen. Palvelu tuotetaan tilaajan osoittamissa toimipisteissä niiden aukioloaikoina erikseen sovittavina kuvausjaksoina. Palvelun tavoitteena on toteuttaa kuvaukset laadukkaasti ja yhdenvertaisesti sekä tunnistaa jatkotutkimuksia ja hoitoa edellyttävät löydökset riittävän varhain. Palvelun tulee olla järjestetty siten, että Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialueen diabeetikoilla on kohtuullinen ja yhdenvertainen mahdollisuus käyttää palvelua. Palveluntuottaja vastaa kuvauslaitteistosta, henkilöstöstä ja palvelun käytännön toteutuksesta tämän palvelukuvauksen mukaisesti. Palvelukokonaisuus muodostuu mm. seuraavista vaiheista: • ajanvaraus ja asiakkaan kutsuminen • silmänpohjakuvaus palveluntuottajan laitteistolla • kuvien arviointi ja lausunto • jatkotoimenpidesuositus sekä kuvien ja lausuntojen toimittaminen sovittuihin järjestelmiin • toiminnan seuranta ja raportointi Tilaajalle,

title: IT Professional Services
description: The Canada Council for the Arts' Information Technology section requires access to qualified professional services providers to support ongoing IT operational requirements and project-based initiatives on an as-and-when-required basis. General requirement The Contractor must provide information technology professional services, on an as-and-when-requested basis, in support of the Canada Council’s operational, maintenance, enhancement, modernization, transformation and advisory requirements. The Contractor must actively support knowledge transfer to Canada Council personnel proportionate to the scope, complexity and duration of each engagement. Deliverables, documentation, training materials, presentations, knowledge transfer activities and related services may be required in English, French or both official languages, as specified in the applicable call-up. The Contractor must provide qualified resources, perform the authorized work and deliver all required outputs in accordance with the requirements of the Standing Offer and the applicable call-up. The Contractor must provide professional services in information technology across one or more of the following service streams: Stream 1 - Enterprise platforms and business applications Services may include the configuration, development, administration, enhancement, integration, maintenance and support of enterprise platforms and business applications, including Microsoft, Salesforce and Unit4 technologies. Stream 2 - Applications, integration and support Services may include the design, development, modernization, testing, deployment, integration, maintenance and support of custom-developed and commercial off-the-shelf applications, interfaces and related components. Stream 3 - Data, analytics and information management Services may include data architecture, data analysis, reporting, analytics, business intelligence, information management, database administration, data governance and data integration. Stream 4 - Architecture, cloud, infrastructure and cybersecurity Services may include enterprise, solution and integration architecture; cloud architecture and infrastructure; cybersecurity; identity and access management; network services; and related advisory, implementation and support activities. Stream 5 - Project, Program and Change Management Support Services may include project and program management, project coordination, business and functional analysis, business process analysis, organizational change management, planning, governance, performance reporting and stakeholder engagement, documentation, knowledge transfer and training services. Stream 6 - User experience, accessibility and quality assurance Services may include user experience design, AI-enabled user experience and service design, accessibility assessment and remediation, testing and quality assurance. Stream 7 - Audit and advisory services Services may include audit and advisory services related to technology controls, compliance, governance, risk management, cybersecurity, platforms, applications, processes and IT operations. Stream 8 - Artificial intelligence, automation and emerging technologies Services may include, in accordance with the Government of Canada's artificial intelligence strategy, artificial intelligence strategy development, generative AI and machine learning advisory services, AI solution design and implementation, responsible AI governance, automation, intelligent search, knowledge management, AI-assisted service delivery, model evaluation, data readiness, and emerging technology assessment.

title: Financial Consultant - Saskatchewan for the Farm Debt Mediation Service (FDMS)
description: The Programs Branch (PB) of Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada (AAFC) has requirements on an “as and when requested” basis for professional resources with expertise and skillsets for the delivery of financial counselling and mediation services. This requirement is to establish a Task Authorization Contract with a qualified Contractor’s for services in Saskatchewan. It is intended to result in the award of 5 (five) contracts for 5 (five) years. The Farm Debt Mediation Service (FDMS) offers free financial counselling and mediation services to farmers who are having difficulties meeting their financial obligations. It is a voluntary, private and confidential service that brings farmers and their creditors together with a Mediator in a neutral forum to reach a mutually acceptable solution. The FDMS Administrator will assign a Financial Consultant and a Mediator to work with the farmer through the mediation process. Confidentiality is extremely important to the quality and effectiveness of the service. Information obtained from the farmer and their creditor(s) is used for the sole purpose of mediation and is shared only among the parties involved in the mediation process. The Financial Consultant will conduct a site visit, inventory all the farmer’s assets, create financial statements of the farming operation, develop a recovery plan for the purpose of reaching a financial arrangement between the farmer and their creditor(s), and attend mediation meeting(s). When the farmer and their creditor(s) agree upon a solution, the Mediator will draw-up an arrangement

title: Cloth, Coated, Nylon/Polyurethane, 235 g/m², CADPAT™ Multi-Terrain (MT) – Re-Tender
description: The Department of National Defence (DND), has a requirement for the production and supply of CADPAT-patterned clothing and associated items for the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF). This solicitation is subject to limited tendering. Only companies holding a valid and active licence to print CADPAT, issued by the Department of National Defence, will be invited to submit bids. The following licensed companies are eligible to participate in this solicitation: • Textiles Monterey (1996) Inc. / Monterey Textiles (1996) Inc. • Brookwood Companies Incorporated • Textil Santanderina, S.A. • NV Utexbel • Brittany Global Technologies Corporation Where a supplier has previously submitted samples to DND for the same or equivalent requirement, those samples may be retained and considered for use in support of the upcoming solicitation, subject to confirmation by DND that they remain representative of the proposed product and continue to meet the applicable technical requirements. Companies interested in obtaining a CADPAT printing licence are invited to contact: Requesting the Commercial Use of the Canadian Disruptive Pattern (CADPAT) - Canada.ca for information regarding the licensing process and eligibility requirements. By limiting the solicitation to organizations that currently hold a valid CADPAT printing licence, DND can ensure compliance with intellectual property, security, and technical requirements associated with the production of CADPAT-patterned materials. Request for Standing Offers (RFSO) package would be provided directly to the eligible licensed firms, increasing the likelihood of receiving compliant and competitive bids. At the same time, transparency is maintained by clearly identifying the eligibility requirements, listing the licensed companies eligible to participate, and providing information for other interested firms wishing to pursue a CADPAT printing licence for future opportunities.

title: Betrieb der hydraulischen Sicherung Deponie Freiheit III – Wartung/ Instandhaltung Pumpen-/ Anlagentechnik
description: Die MDSE betreibt als Projektträgerin auf Grundlage einer behördlichen Anordnung dauerhaft die hydraulische Sicherung der Deponie Freiheit III und ist für die ordnungsgemäße Hebung/ Sammlung/ Ableitung anfallender Grund-/ Oberflächenwässer aus dem Deponiebereich verantwortlich. Bei den Hebungswässern handelt es sich geogen/ anthropogen bedingt um stark mineralisierte Wässer, die zu erheblichen Ausfällungen und Ablagerungen (vorwiegend Eisen(III)-hydroxid (braun), aber auch Eisen(II)-sulfid (schwarz)) im gesamten Ableitungssystem führen. Um die Funktionstüchtigkeit der Gefahrenabwehrmaßnahme der hydraulischen Sicherung der Deponie Freiheit III jederzeit zu gewährleisten, sind Arbeiten zur Wartung/ Instandhaltung der Pumpen-/ Anlagentechnik erforderlich. Diese Leistungen werden von der MDSE vergeben und sind Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung.

title: Palvelimien turvasäilö
description: Palvelimien turvasäilö Hankinnan kohteena on ratkaisu, jonka avulla voidaan tarjota tietoturvallisesti eristetty ja hallittu palvelinsäilö varmuuskopioidulle datalle. Ratkaisun tulee mahdollistaa varmuuskopioiden turvallinen säilytys, käsittely ja hyödyntäminen erillisessä, tuotantoympäristöstä irrotetussa kokonaisuudessa. TIETOJENKÄSITTELYN OIKEUTUS, SIJAINTI, HALLINTAYHTEYDET JA SUOJAUS Hankinnan kohteena oleva palvelimen turvasäilö -palvelu sisältää Tilaajan varmistusympäristöstä replikoitavaa varmistusdataa, joka voi sisältää Tilaajan oman datan ohella myös mm. omistaja-asiakkaiden potilastietojärjestelmien tietoja ja siten EU:n yleisen tietosuoja-asetuksen 9 artiklassa tarkoitettuja erityisiin henkilötietoryhmiin kuuluvia henkilötietoja. Erityisiin henkilötietoryhmiin kuuluvien tietojen käsittely on lähtökohtaisesti kiellettyä, mutta käsittely on sallittua, kun kieltoon on säädetty poikkeus. Tässä palvelussa käsittely on välttämätöntä terveydenhuollon tietojärjestelmien ja palvelujen hallinnoimiseksi sekä palvelujen jatkuvuuden ja palautettavuuden varmistamiseksi (GDPR 9(2)(h)). Käsittely toteutetaan omistaja-asiakkaiden (rekisterinpitäjien) ohjeiden mukaisesti; Tilaaja toimii henkilötietojen käsittelijänä ja vastaa alikäsittelijöiden (Toimittaja mahdollisine alihankkijoineen) hallinnasta. Rekisterinpitäjien osoitusvelvollisuuden, valvottavuuden ja käsiteltävien tietojen korkean suojaustason varmistamiseksi Tilaaja edellyttää, että: 1) varmistusdata säilytetään ja sitä käsitellään yksinomaan Suomen alueella sijaitsevissa konesaleissa, ja 2) myös palvelun hallintayhteydet (ylläpito- ja hallintaliikenne sekä mahdolliset etähallintaratkaisut) ovat sallittuja vain Suomen alueelta, ja 3) varmistusdata on salattuna (siirrossa ja levossa) ja palvelu tuotetaan ainoastaan Tilaajalle dedikoidussa ympäristössä. Vaatimus on rajattu koskemaan vain hankinnan kohteena olevaa varmistuspalvelua ja on oikeassa suhteessa hankinnan tavoitteeseen ja käsiteltävien tietojen luonteeseen nähden. OPTIO Optiona pyydetään hinnoittelua analytiikkapalvelulle (Eristetty analytiikkaympäristö ransomware- ja virusskannauksineen), joka toimii täysin erillisessä verkkovyöhykkeessä ilman pääsyä tuotantoverkkoon. Kyseistä palvelua voidaan hankkia sopimusaikana tarpeen mukaan, minkä vuoksi se on vertailuhinnassa mukana vain yhden vuoden osalta.,

title: Visit Finland UK matkailun markkinaedustaja/Visit Finland UK market travel trade representation
description: Visit Finland UK matkailun markkinaedustaja/Visit Finland UK market travel trade representation BELOW IN ENGLISH: Business Finland Oy (myöhemmin "Business Finland/BF/hankintayksikkö") pyytää tarjoustanne Visit Finland UK:n markkinaedustajasta tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti vuosille 2027-2028 (optio vuodelle 2029). Hankinnan kohteena on Visit Finlandin B2B-läsnäolon tukeminen Ison-Britannian markkinoilla. Visit Finland hakee tukea suomalaisen matkailuelinkeinon kannalta relevanttien matkailualan verkostosuhteiden rakentamiseen ja ylläpitämiseen, erityisesti keskittyen Suomen tunnettuuden lisäämiseen kesäkohteena Ison-Britannian matkailualan yleisön keskuudessa. Valittava toimittaja toimii Visit Finlandin markkina-edustajana Isossa-Britanniassa ja on siten vastuussa Suomen yleisen läsnäolon ylläpitämisestä asiaankuuluvilla matkailualan alustoilla. Toimittaja toimii Visit Finlandin puolesta ensisijaisena yhteyshenkilönä Ison-Britannian matkailumarkkinoilla. Toimittajan odotetaan ylläpitävän säännöllistä, ennakoivaa ja jatkuvaa vuorovaikutusta keskeisten jakelukanavien, matkanjärjestäjien, matkatoimistojen, online-matkatoimistojen, lentoyhtiökumppaneiden ja muiden asiaankuuluvien matkailualan sidosryhmien kanssa Ison-Britannian markkinoilla. Toimittajan on aktiivisesti tunnistettava markkinamahdollisuuksia, ylläpidettävä vahvoja toimialasuhteita ja edistettävä tehokasta viestintää Visit Finlandin ja Ison-Britannian matkailualan kumppaneiden välillä. Tällä hetkellä UK:ssa ei ole edustajaa vaan markkinaa on johdettu Suomesta käsin. Tavoitteena on löytää UK:n markkinalle ulkoinen palveluntarjoaja 1.1.2027 alkaen. Mikäli tarjouspyyntöasiakirjojen suomenkielisen ja englanninkielisen version välillä ilmenee ristiriitaa, epäselvyyttä tai tulkintaeroja, ensisijaisesti sovelletaan englanninkielistä versiota. Tarkempi hankinnan kohteen kuvaus löytyy tarjouspyynnön liitteestä 1. Materiaalit ovat pääosin ainoastaan englanniksi. Kaikkien tarjousasiakirjojen on oltava englanniksi. SOPIMUSKAUSI Sopimuskauden kesto on 2 vuotta (2027-2028) + optio vuodelle 2029. Optio otetaan käyttöön vain tarpeen mukaan. Optio on mahdollista ottaa käyttöön kokonaan tai kuukausi kerrallaan. Option mahdollisesta käyttöönotosta ilmoitetaan kirjallisesti viimeistään kahta (2) kuukautta ennen sopimuskauden päättymistä. HANKINNAN LAAJUUS Hankinnan arvioitu arvo on noin 180 000 euroa (alv 0 %) sisältäen optiokauden vuodelle 2029 sekä palvelumaksun, lisätehtävät, valinnaiset palvelut (optiot) sekä enintään 10 000 euroa vuodessa pieniin toimintakuluihin. Hankinta ylittää julkisista hankinnoista ja käyttöoikeussopimuksista annetussa laissa (1397/2016) säädetyn kansallisen kynnysarvon, mutta jää alle EU-kynnysarvon. Tarjoajaa pyydetään huomioimaan, että tarjousten jättöaika on ilmoitettu Suomen ajassa. ****************************** Business Finland Oy (hereinafter referred to as "Business Finland/BF/Contracting Entity") invites your tender for the Visit Finland UK market representative in accordance with this call for tenders and its annexes for the years 2027-2028 (option for year 2029). The subject of the procurement is to support Visit Finland´s B2B presence in the UK market. Visit Finland seeks for support for building and maintaining the relationships with the travel trade network relevant to Finnish travel trade and especially focusing on building Finland’s awareness as a summer destination among the UK travel trade audience. The selected partner will work as the market representative for Visit Finland in the UK and therefore has the responsibility for maintaining the overall presence of Finland in relevant travel trade platforms. The Supplier shall act as the primary point of contact for the UK travel trade market on behalf of Visit Finland. The Supplier is expected to maintain frequent, proactive, and continuous engagement with key distribution channels, tour operators, travel agents, OTAs, airline partners, and other relevant travel trade stakeholders in the UK market. The Supplier shall actively identify market opportunities, maintain strong industry relationships, and facilitate effective communication between Visit Finland and UK travel trade partners. Visit Finland currently does not have a representative in the UK, but the market has previously been managed from Finland. The goal is to find an external service provider for the UK market starting January 1, 2027. In the event of any conflict, inconsistency, or discrepancy between the Finnish-language and English-language versions of the procurement documents, the English-language version shall prevail. A more detailed description of the procurement object can be found in Appendix 1 of the Call for Tenders. The materials are primarily available only in English. All tender documents must be in English. CONTRACT PERIOD The contract period is 2 years (2027-2028) + option for year 2029. The option will only be used as needed. Visit Finland may exercise the option period either in full or in part, on a month-by-month basis. Any possible use of the option will be notified in writing no later than two (2) months before the end of the contract period. SCOPE OF THE PROCUREMENT The estimated value of the procurement is approximately 180,000 euros (VAT 0 %) including an option period for the year 2029, as well as service fees, additional tasks, optional services (options), and up to 10,000 euros per year for minor operating expenses. Please note that the deadline for submitting tenders is stated in Finnish time.,

The Contractor shall complete and provide the checklist in accordance with DFARs 252.215-7009 identifying whether each of the criteria are met and provide a copy with the submission of the proposal. For major subcontracts over $10,000,000, please include a completed cost and pricing analysis in accordance with FAR 15.404-3(b). In the event that the Contractor or any of its subcontractors have non-complying existing deficiencies, the Government requests that these deficiencies be reported to the PCO as soon as they are known. **Instructions for submitting the DD2345 and details applicable to the evaluation criteria are included in the Buy Terms attached in this solicitation.** **Please submit all proposals no later than 23 November 2026 at 9 AM to Molly Jackson (molly.s.jackson.civ@us.navy.mil).*

title: APN - BASE JANITORIAL SERVICES CFB SHILO, MANITOBA
description: Advance Procurement Notice BASE JANITORIAL SERVICES CFB SHILO, MANITOBA (with Security Requirements) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at CFB Shilo, Shilo Manitoba. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Description of the Project and Services The Department of National Defence and Defence Construction Canada intends to put in place a contract to provide all labour, material, supervision and equipment to supply janitorial services at CFB Shilo, Manitoba.  In general, the work includes, but not limited to: Janitorial cleaning services (internal and external elements) General Requirements wipe down benches, exercise equipment and weight machines; dusting of blinds; vacuuming of curtains and drapery; cleaning/stocking of dispensers; clean & disinfect door handles, handrails and switch plates cleaning and disinfecting of drinking fountains; spot clean/ replace of entrance mats and grates; floor strip/refinishing; sweep/vacuum and damp mop of flooring; vacuum (automatic type) pools; clean and disinfect pool deck; clean, damp mop and disinfect sauna room; cleaning and disinfect bathroom fixtures; waste removal; glass cleaning Other Tasks carpet/furniture shampooing and steam cleaning The approximate estimated cost for these services is $4,000,000.00 over two (2) years with the potential for three (3) additional one (1) year extensions and an increase in value up to $6,000,000.00. The estimated total potential value is approximately $10,000,000.00 over a possible five (5) year period. It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. Contract Number:  SLSO2796 Title: Base Janitorial Services Total Potential Value: $10,000,000.00 Anticipated Posting: November 2026 Anticipated Contract Commencement: April 2027 Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for contract award, a bidder will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a bid for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential bidders with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, consultants or contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number (Project number on the MERX notice); Contract number SLSO2796; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored for. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the consultants or contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a consultant or contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation (Contract number listed on their request for sponsorship) being advertised on MERX, has  met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package, and has submitted a proposal or a bid DCC will  send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or bidder regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent or bidder will need to promptly cooperate with CSP  to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Brad Jeaurond Coordinator, Contract Services Defence Construction Canada 204-765-3000, ext. 258-4094 Bradley.Jeaurond@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent or bidder agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the bidder or proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated  sponsorship process.Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

title: Ersatzbeschaffung Beatmungsgeräte Intensivstation
description: Die Intensivstation des Universitäts-Kinderspitals Zürich – Eleonorenstiftung ersetzt ihre aktuellen Flotte an Beatmungsgeräten durch 24 Apparate der neusten Generation, welche das gesamtes Alters- und Gewichtsspektrum der behandelten PatientInnen abdeckt. Der Umfang beinhaltet nebst den Ventilatoren ein Transportgestell, die Atemgasbefeuchtung, Anschlüsse / Schnittstellen (PDMS, Gas), Verbrauchsmaterial, sowie einen Service-Vertrag und Schulungen durch den / die HerstellerIn. Der Projektleiter Dr. med. Jürg Martin Burren deklariert, für Weiterbildungen an Kursen der Firma Hamilton Speaker Fees für Vorträge zu den Themen "pädiatrisches ARDS" und "Beatmungs-Weaning bei pädiatrischen PatientInnen" in Form von Drittmittelgeldern auf ein Konto des Kinderspitals Zürich, Eleonorenstiftung - erhalten zu haben. Das Bewertungsteam besteht aus 18 Personen. Eine detaillierte Auflistung ist im Reiter «Dokumente» im Word-Dokument «Projektgruppe Ersatzbeschaffung Beatmungsgeräte IPS KISPI 2026» hinterlegt.

title: USZ Campus MITTE 1|2 / CVC 277.30 Salle Blanche
description: L'hôpital universitaire de Zurich (USZ) prévoit une rénovation complète de la zone centrale. Le projet Campus MITTE1|2 (CM1|2) constitue la première étape de la rénovation structurelle globale de l'USZ. Le projet comprend le démantèlement de plusieurs bâtiments, la construction d'un nouveau bâtiment MITTE 1|2 d'environ 44 mètres de haut et la rénovation/conversion de l'ancienne anatomie.

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Zweiphasiger städtebaulich-freiraumplanerischer Wettbewerb nach RPW 2013 - Produktives Quartier Gutleut-West
description: Gegenstand des Wettbewerbes ist ein städtebaulich-freiraumplanerischer Entwurf in dem gezeigt wird, wie die Transformation eines gewerblich geprägten Bestandsareals zu einem nutzungsgemischten, klimaangepassten und gemeinwohlorientierten Quartier gelingen kann. In einer Stadt mit hoher Flächennachfrage und begrenzten innerstädtischen Entwicklungsreserven treffen hier Ansprüche unmittelbar aufeinander, die sich andernorts oft räumlich aus dem Weg gehen: Wohnen und Gewerbe, Logistik und Aufenthalt, soziale Infrastruktur und Produktion, Freiraum und Verdichtung. Die entscheidende Frage lautet deshalb nicht, welche Nutzung sich am Ende durchsetzt. Interessanter ist, wie aus dieser Konkurrenz ein Stück Stadt entstehen kann. Aufgabe des Wettbewerbs ist es, eine eigene räumliche Antwort zu entwickeln. Gesucht wird vornehmlich nicht das möglichst vollständige Bild eines irgendwann „fertigen“ Gutleut-West. Gesucht wird vielmehr ein städtebauliches und freiraumplanerisches Gerüst, das Orientierung gibt, ohne Entwicklung einzuschränken. Es soll durch zu entwickelnde Prinzipien Qualitäten sichern und zugleich Spielräume eröffnen – für unterschiedliche Nutzungen, Träger:innen, Eigentümer:innen und Entwicklungszeitpunkte. Die Ausloberin beabsichtigt, unter Würdigung der Empfehlung des Preisgerichts, das mit dem 1. Preis ausgezeichnete Team mit der Ausarbeitung des Wettbewerbsergebnisses zu beauftragen. Die Ausloberin wird hierzu ein Verhandlungsverfahren ohne Teilnahmewettbewerb gemäß § 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 8 VgV durchführen. Dabei behält sich die Ausloberin vor, das Verhandlungsverfahren zunächst nur mit dem mit dem 1. Preis ausgezeichneten Team durchzuführen. Scheitern diese Verhandlungen oder besteht ein wichtiger Grund, der einer Beauftragung des 1. Preisträgers entgegensteht, werden die weiteren Preisträger zur Teilnahme an den Verhandlungen aufgefordert. Das Wettbewerbsergebnis wird im anschließenden Vergabeverfahren als Zuschlagskriterium mit 60 % gewichtet. Die Rangfolge der Preisträger gemäß der Entscheidung des Preisgerichts wird dabei entsprechend berücksichtigt, d.h. der 1. Preisträger erhält im Kriterium ‚Wettbewerbsergebnis' die höchste Punktzahl, der 2. Preisträger die zweithöchste usw. Die weitere Bearbeitung umfasst den städtebaulichen Entwurf nach Merkblatt Nr. 51 der Architektenkammer Baden-Württemberg, Honorarzone IV, Leistungsphasen 1–3 sowie den freiräumlichen Entwurf nach Merkblatt Nr. 52 der Architektenkammer Baden-Württemberg, Honorarzone IV, Leistungsphasen 1–3 sowie die Erstellung eines "Qualitätshandbuchs". Eine darüberhinausgehende Beauftragung weiterer Planungsleistungen bleibt vorbehalten und ist nicht Bestandteil dieses Auftragsversprechens. Ziel ist die Erarbeitung eines Rahmenplans mit integrierter Freiraumplanung als Vorstufe zum Bebauungsplan nach BauGB sowie als Grundlage für das im Anschluss geplante Konzeptverfahren für die hochbauliche Entwicklung auf den Baufeldern. Die Preisträger:innen verpflichten sich, im Falle einer Beauftragung durch die Ausloberin, die weitere Bearbeitung zu übernehmen und durchzuführen. Im Zuge der Überarbeitung der Wettbewerbsergebnisse treten sie mit der Bürgerschaft und Schlüsselpersonen vor Ort im Rahmen von Dialogformaten in Austausch (z.B. Vorstellung des Wettbewerbs-Ergebnisses, Rückfragenbeantwortung, Aufnahme von Hinweisen für weitere Bearbeitung). Die Beauftragung erfolgt vorbehaltlich des Abschlusses des erforderlichen Vergabeverfahrens, der erforderlichen haushaltsrechtlichen Voraussetzungen, der Eignung des Teilnehmers sowie des Vorliegens eines wichtigen Grundes, der einer Beauftragung entgegensteht. Im Falle einer weiteren Bearbeitung werden durch den Wettbewerb bereits erbrachte Leistungen des Preisträgers bis zur Höhe des zuerkannten Preises nicht erneut vergütet, wenn und soweit der Wettbewerbsentwurf unverändert der weiteren Bearbeitung zugrunde gelegt wird.

title: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation for Spent Fuel Cell Shipment(s)
description: Amendment 01: The response due date has been extended from November 5, 2026 to November 23, 2026. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Center for Neutron Research (NCNR) owns and operates a 20 MW test reactor called the National Bureau of Standards Reactor (NBSR) located in Gaithersburg, Maryland. The NBSR is fueled by 30 highly enriched uranium fuel elements. During the course of a year, the NBSR produces approximately 28 spent fuel elements. To be in accordance with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), NIST is required to transfer its spent fuel to the Department of Energy (DOE) Savannah River Site (SRS) near Aiken, South Carolina. This requirement is for one base shipment to be completed no later than December 31, 2028, with an option for a second shipment to be completed no later than December 31, 2030. title: Solid-State Energy Conversion from Heat to Electricity Request for Information (RFI)
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Defense Sciences Office (DSO) is requesting information on the current state of the art and technological limitations of solid-state direct thermal-to-electric energy conversion technologies. We define solid state energy conversion as systems that convert a temperature differential directly into electrical energy without utilizing mechanical moving parts (e.g., pistons, turbines, or rotary alternators). This RFI seeks to identify the best possible solid state heat engine performance across a wide operating temperature range, factors that limit performance, and the most attractive use cases if these highly efficient solid state heat engines could be made today. This survey of limits, challenges and use cases will identify opportunities for research and development to inform potential program(s) in this area.

description: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE AEC11 Source control (design bid build) 19 wing, CFB Comox, Lazo, BC (with security requirements) 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at 19 Wing, CFB Comox, Lazo, BC. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. title: Canonsburg-Houston, Pennsylvania, Local Protection Project (LPP) PL84-99 Rehabilitation
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Pittsburgh District, has a project as the Canonsburg-Houston Local Protection Project (LPP) is an authorized federal flood damage reduction project spanning over 20,500 linear feet of channel improvements along Chartiers Creek. Originally constructed by USACE in two phases (Houston unit completed in 1970; Canonsburg unit completed in 1976), operation and maintenance responsibilities were subsequently transferred to Washington County. Severe storm events resulted in substantial damage to the channel embankment along the right bank of Chartiers Creek, including displacement of stone protection and loss of subgrade stabilization. This rehabilitation contract encompasses repair and re-armoring of the degraded channel reach to restore federal project integrity and design conveyance capacity. The work is to be completed within 365 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed (NTP). The Anticipated Construction Cost is between $150,000.00 and $350,000.00. The North American Industrial Classification Code (NAICS) is 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The Small Business Size Standard is $45,000,000.00. Any resultant award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Purchase Order. The anticipated award date is 11 December 2026. The basis of award will be of best value to the Government. Quotes will be evaluated in accordance with (IAW) RFO Part 13 and 36, price and past performance. The Government reserves the right to reject any quotes that are unrealistically low or exceed available funds for this requirement. title: Float Well Pipe Repairs, Surry Mountain Dam, Surry, NH
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is issuing this Sources Sought Announcement for Construction Services for the for the repairing of the inlet pipe to the float well and replace weathered/damaged staff gauges at the Surry Moutain Lake Dam in Surry NH. This announcement is to determine interest, availability and capability of 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Women-Owned and Small Business concerns for this project. The NAICS code for this procurement is 237990 with a size standard of $45M. The project is planned to be solicited in the Winter of 2026 with construction to begin place in the Summer of 2027. The estimated construction cost is between $350,000 - $500,000. The project site is the inlet culvert on the lake side of the Surry Mountain Dam in Surry, NH. Work for this project will likely include, but not be limited to, the following: Coffer dam at inlet pipe location. Float well pipe (3-inch cast iron) cleaning. Installation of internal liner for float well pipe. Pre and Post liner installation CCTV inspections. Repairs to the slash-zone pipe segment Protection and concrete encasement of the external float well pipe Staff Gauges: Pressure treated posts with attached enamel coated metal measuring strip. Scheduled work will be affected by depth of pool. Assumed low pool depths are July and August (when work can be conducted safely), but adverse weather conditions (rain events) could delay or postpone work schedules. Surry Mountain staff will keep COR informed of pool levels to anticipate when work can commence if outside assumed low pool depths. Interested firms should submit a capabilities package to include the following: business classification (i.e. HUBZone, small business, etc.), as well as qualifications and experience in performing the work components stated above. Please include at least two specific examples of the firm�s experience performing the work requirements stated above. The projects must have been performed within the last seven years. Please indicate the team subcontractor(s) (if any), including their prior experience and qualifications, which will be used to support the offeror�s effort, and their experience must also have been performed within the last seven years. Proof of bonding capability is required. Responses are limited to twenty pages. Responses are due by 21 September 2026. Responses should be emailed to: Kyle Hall � kyle.k.hall@usace.army.mil Phone Contact: (978) 318-8479 Interested firms shall provide the above documentation in one original form and one copy. The Government will not pay for any material provided in response to this market survey nor return the data provided. This notice is for information purposes only and is not a request to be placed on a solicitation mailing list nor is it a Request for Proposal (RFP) or an announcement of a solicitation. The results of this survey will be considered to be in effect for a period of one year from the date of this notice. Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR)
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-209, located at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, is seeking information from potential sources regarding a modular Software Defined Radio (SDR) for U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft, designated the Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR). The NGTR is intended to support voice and data waveforms in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands, with operational capability extending up to 6 GHz. It will incorporate a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) to meet National Security Agency (NSA) cryptographic and Security Evaluation Requirements Document (SERD) requirements. Additionally, the NGTR is designed to serve as a form, fit, and function backwards-compatible replacement for aircraft currently equipped with the ARC-210 Generation 5 and Generation 6 radios. This Market Research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Request for Information (RFI) will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this RFI is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the RFP. The following documents are attached to this RFI Notice: Attachment 1: NGTR RFI Performance Requirements - DRAFT Attachment 2: Program and Risk Feedback Matrix The following dates are anticipated time frames associated with this requirement: Estimated Industry Day: 1st Quarter FY27 Estimated Draft RFP Release: 3rd Quarter FY 27 Estimated Final RFP Release: 4th Quarter FY 27 Estimated Award Date: 2nd Quarter FY 28 Target Fleet Delivery: Mid-2034 � Production-ready NGTR systems delivered to fleet locations for aircraft installation Primary Place of Performance: Contractor facility and as needed at government test sites and government facilities for meetings with NAVAIR and NSA. 2.0 DISCLAIMER THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS REQUEST IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND The NGTR system's goal is to develop a small form factor system compatible with existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft that will support: Communications waveforms in the VHF, UHF frequency bands with support for waveforms up to 6GHz. Waveforms defined in Attachment 1. A Modular, Open architecture to support rapid capability integration and obsolescence upgrades including a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) that supports NSA cryptographic and SERD requirements. Zero Trust System security meeting applicable Risk Management Framework (RMF) controls. Minimal integration impact and modification requirements for existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft platforms. 4.0 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The NGTR system is expected to meet the performance requirements defined in Attachment 1: �NGTR RFI Performance Requirements� - DRAFT. The NGTR Contractor is expected to meet the following qualifications: Have secure military software defined radios with embedded NSA certified cryptography. Have experience in agile and modular development and testing, incorporating customer feedback throughout the process. Have the ability to obtain Top Secret security clearances for employees and facility within 12 months of contract award, including the ability to support development and test up to the Top Secret level. Have experience in developing and producing UHF and VHF RF radios supporting military and non-military communications waveforms. Has experience in Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). Have expertise and experience in reducing total life cycle support costs and utilizing predictive maintenance strategies to streamline repair procedures and reduce maintenance downtime. Have experience establishing, maintaining, and documenting a proactive DMSMS (Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages) and obsolescence programs. 5.0 ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing), with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,250 Employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 5821, (Radio and Television Communication Equipment, Airborne). Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. Note: FAR 52.219-14 Limitation on Subcontracting requires a small business prime on a Set-Aside to perform at least 50% of the cost of contract performance. Small business primes may now count �first tier subcontracted� work performed by similarly situated entities as if it were performed by the prime itself. To assist in market research and determination of any applicable small business set-aside for this effort, small businesses interested in priming this effort and planning to use �similarly situated entities� to meet the Limitations on Subcontracting, are requested to identify: The name & CAGE Code of the specific firm(s) intending to partner/subcontract Their small business size status under the NAICS that as the prime, you would assign for their workshare. 6.0 SUBMISSION DETAILS To ensure a fair, orderly, and efficient evaluation process, all interested parties must adhere to the following submission guidelines: 6.1 Logistics and Deadlines Response Date: All submissions must be received no later than 2:00 PM EST on 23 November 2026. Questions Deadline: Clarifying questions regarding this RFI must be submitted via email no later than 10 business days prior to the response date. 6.2 Submission Method and Point of Contact (POC) Delivery: Submissions must be sent via Electronic-mail (Email) to the Contract Specialist, Sham Keswani, at sham.v.keswani.civ@us.navy.mil. Subject Line Format: The email subject line must read: NGTR RFI Response - [Company Name]. Inquiries: No phone calls will be accepted. All questions must be submitted via email to the Contract Specialist listed above. 6.3 Format and Structure Instructions Page Limit: Submissions must not exceed ten (10) pages total (excluding the Program and Risk Feedback Matrix in Section 7.0). Page Size & Margins: Standard 8.5 x 11-inch pages with 1-inch margins. Font: Times New Roman, font size of not less than 10 point. Document Type: Adobe PDF format. Classification: No classified information shall be submitted in response to this RFI. 6.4 Required Content Your submission package must include the following structured sections: Cover Page / Company Profile: Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, DUNS/UEI, Business Size Status under NAICS 334220, and designated Points of Contact (POC) including names, phone numbers, and email addresses. Capabilities Statement: A detailed narrative addressing your ability to meet the special requirements and required capabilities outlined in Section 4.0. Program and Risk Feedback: Completed responses to the targeted questions and the structured feedback matrix outlined in Section 7.0. 6.5 Proprietary Data and Information Handling All data received in response to this RFI that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the Government. Any information or materials provided in response to this RFI Notice will not be returned. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to identify business concerns with sufficient similar experience that are capable and interested in performing the work described herein. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Norfolk District is anticipating a new procurement for a Firm-Fixed Price Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Services contract, for the Department of War Education Activity (DoWEA) Preventative Maintenance (PM) and Demand Maintenance (DM) at Ft. Buchanan, San Juan and Ramey Unit School, Aguadilla, Puerto Rico. Description of Work USACE, Norfolk District is seeking eligible firms capable of Preventative Maintenance and Demand Maintenance repair services in support of the DoWEA-America�s facilities located at Ft. Buchanan, San Juan and Ramey Unit School, Aguadilla, Puerto Rico. The services provided under this proposed contract encompass facilities total maintenance services such as operation and maintenance of heating, ventilation and cooling systems, kitchen equipment, facility control systems, playgrounds, plumbing, electrical, and fire alarms, building systems, roofs, and other facility systems and components. These services must be provided on an ongoing basis without protracted lapse to ensure that the building systems continue to operate efficiently and safely for the benefit of the students and teachers that inhabit them. The facilities under this action which require Preventative Maintenance & Demand Repair Maintenance include a total of five (5) buildings comprised of three (3) schools and one (1) support facility at Ft. Buchanan, San Juan for an approximate total of 320,870 GSF; and one (1) Ramey Unit School at Aguadilla for an approximate total of 122,539 GSF. Solicitation Anticipated solicitation issuance timeframe is on or about January 2027, and the estimated solicitation period of 30 calendar days with a proposal due date timeframe on or about February 2027. The project consists of a 12-month base period, four (4) option years for a total of five (5) years. NAICS Code 238220 - Plumbing, Heating, and Air-Conditioning Contractors applies with a Small Business Size Standard of $19,000,000.00 Offerors will be evaluated on a Best-Value Tradeoff basis with a combination of price and non-price factors. All interested firms shall be registered in SAM.GOV and PIEE in order to submit a proposal in response to the solicitation when issued. VIRTUAL INDUSTRY DAY NOTICE The Government will host a Virtual Industry Day to engage with interested parties and address questions related to this requirement. Participation in the Virtual Industry Day is voluntary and is not required to submit a capabilities statement. The Virtual Industry Day will be held on Monday, 16 NOV 2026 from 0900-1000 AM Eastern Standard Time (EST). A Microsoft Teams meeting invite will be provided to interested firms who RSVP by email no later than 12 NOV 2026 to Susan Ellis at susan.k.ellis@usace.army.mil and Nicholas Lizotte at nicholas.lizotte@usace.army.mil. INFORMATION REQUESTED FROM INDUSTRY All interested, capable, qualified, and responsive SMALL BUSINESS Prime Contractors are encouraged to reply to this Sources Sought announcement. Interested contractors should furnish the following information: Company name, address, phone number, and point of contact information. Indicate business size in relation to the NAICS Code 238220. Provide your company's Unique Entity Identification number (UEI) to verify your business status as a qualified Small Business (SB), Service-Disabled Veteran Owned SB (SDVOSB), Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZones), Qualified Section 8(a), Women-Owned or other than Small Business. Contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at time of proposal submission and contract award. Please see www.SAM.gov for additional registration information. Provide a narrative describing primary business lines and the geographic regions your company serves. Narratives shall be no longer than five (5) pages demonstrating experience in a similar type of work as described above, at similar contract values, and in similar locations. Does your company, through in-house forces or subcontract support, have the technical capability and capacity to provide preventive maintenance and demand maintenance repair services for the facilities and locations as described above? Given the Facility Coverage requirements listed in the description of work: what level of staffing would you suggest for full-time employees to be on-site (full time) to fulfill these requirements. Please include the trades as well as the personnel�s pertinent certifications/licenses. The Government intends to include a Limit of Liability (LOL) in this contract for repairs the Contractor would be responsible for under the firm-fixed price portion of this contract. The Contractor�s limit of liability (LoL) for material and labor costs associated with any single demand maintenance event including repair or replacement of any single piece of equipment is $20,000 without limit of maintenance occurrences per year. The Government will utilize this information in determining an Acquisition Strategy. Please submit capability packages electronically via email to Susan Ellis at susan.k.ellis@usace.army.mil and copy Nicholas Lizotte at nicholas.lizotte@usace.army.mil. The capability statement must be submitted not later than 23 NOV 2026 by 2:00 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST). This Sources Sought should not be construed in any manner to be an obligation of USACE, Norfolk District to issue a contract, or result in any claim for reimbursement of costs for any effort you expend responding to this request. All information submitted will be considered procurement sensitive and is being used as a market research tool only. No solicitation is currently available. All prospective contractors are required to be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database prior to proposal submission and award. Offerors and contractors may obtain information on registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the Internet at https://www.SAM.gov. Representations and Certifications Applications apply to this solicitation. Representations and Certifications may be completed online via SAM.gov. The Point of Contact for this requirement is Susan Ellis at susan.k.ellis@usace.army.mil, and Nicholas Lizotte at nicholas.lizotte@usace.army.mil. TELEPHONE INQUIRES WILL NOT BE HONORED.

title: Manufacture of M284A2 155mm and other MTC Cannon Tubes
description: Purpose: The Army Contracting Command - Rock Island (ACC-RI) at Picatinny, Picatinny Arsenal, NJ 07806-5000 is conducting a Market Survey on behalf of the Project Manager Howitzer Systems (PM-HS). PM-HS has a need to identify potential sources capable of manufacturing the M284A2 155mm, and other 155mm cannon tubes domestically in specific quantities and lead time annotated below. The purpose of this market research is to obtain current information on the capability of additional sources to manufacture 155mm Cannon Tubes up to 30-foot length. No other data or drawings will be provided with this Market Survey. Description: The .39 caliber, 155-mm M776 and M284A2 cannon tubes are components of the M777A2 and M109A6/A7 Howitzers respectively. 155-mm cannons are direct support cannon fire support system for the U.S. Army and must be built to the United States Government technical data specifications. This Sources Sought is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation or an obligation on the part of the US Government. All interested respondents are requested to provide a written response summarizing the following capabilities and organizational details. Manufacturers with domestic capacity in the works are also encouraged submit their response along with their prospective production timetables. Please clarify if respondent�s capabilities apply to one or all the cannon tube models. REQUESTED: 1. Name of company, address, telephone number, email address, technical point of contact, CAGE code, UEI, and business size information (please specify as either a Large Business, Foreign-Owned Business, Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, 8(a) concern, Woman-Owned Small Business, Historically Underutilized Business Zone concern, Veteran-Owned Small Business, or Service-Disabled Small Business). 2. Experience: A description of the respondent�s manufacturing experience of the 155-mm Cannon Tubes, or similar products, within the last five (5) years to include past performance. Include applicable description of experience with each cannon tube. 3. Production Process: A description of the respondent�s existing 155-mm cannon production process to include all major manufacturing stages and the operations/equipment utilized for each, as well as all supporting subcontractors. The description must detail the entire production lifecycle, including, but not limited to: 3.1. A detailed description of the respondents bore and outside diameter cold working capabilities to include autofrettage. 3.2. A detailed description of the respondent�s boring and milling capabilities along with the capacity or each (length, weight, outer/inner diameters). 3.3. A detailed description of the respondent's rifling capabilities, including methods (e.g., swage, broach, or single-point machining) and general experience with standard 155-mm rifling configurations (lands, grooves, and twist rates). 3.4. A detailed description of the respondent or subcontractor coating capabilities for chrome bore coatings on a steel tube up to 30 ft long and up to 7,500 pounds in weight. Provide the maximum length and weight of tube that can be coated by respondent. 3.5. A detailed description of the respondent�s protective coating and painting capabilities. 3.6. Detailed description of the respondent�s advanced manufacturing capabilities and growth areas. 4. Production Capacity: A description of the respondent�s current maximum monthly capacity to produce 155-mm cannon tubes. Please specify separate production rate capacity for each and if different manufacturing lines, tooling, or subcontractors are utilized. 5. Production Availability: A description of the respondent�s maximum caliber capability and projected available capacity to produce 155-mm cannon tubes within 18 months from the date of these sources sought. 6. Optimization opportunity: A description of the domestic facilities, equipment, machines and tooling required to increase the available capacity to produce 155-mm cannon tubes up to ten (10) tubes per month, regardless of caliber, within 36 months from the date of this source sought. Specify whether the projected production capacity for each tube type is dedicated or shared across multiple lines. Provide an NTE ROM cost estimate for an initial production quantity of forty (40) cannon tubes (broken down by caliber or indicating pricing for a combined/flexible mix). 7. Material: A detailed description of the respondent�s cannon tube source material grade, respondent(s) and processing. Such as, but not limited to, steel preform production, forging, guide bore, and heat treatment. All companies interested in this notice must be registered and valid in System for Award Management (SAM). This market survey is for informational and planning purposes and shall NOT be construed as a Request for Proposal (RFP). All information is to be submitted at no cost or obligation to the Government. If a future formal Government requirement is generated, a solicitation notice will be published. Please identify, with markings, proprietary information submitted. All respondents� information provided will not be returned, will hold in confidential status, and destruction notice shall be provided. All market information sought in this notification must be provided within 30 days of this notice by electronic mail only at no cost to the Government.

When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. If finished detail drawings are not available, shop drawings in the form used by the manufacturer will be acceptable for Government evaluation. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. title: B-52 Data Interface Unit/Data Transfer Receptacle (DTR) - Buy and Repair F3I DTR
description: B-52 Data Interface Unit/Data Transfer Receptacle (DTR) The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources with the expertise, capabilities, experience, facilities, and technical capacity necessary to manufacture/provide and repair the B-52 Data Interface Unit/Data Transfer Receptacle (DTR). The National Stock Number (NSN) and Part Number (PN) are as follows: LRU: NSN 7025-01-738-4504AY, P/N P210015K0001-1, INTERFACE UNIT, DATA This Request for Information (RFI) supports a buy and repair requirement for the new Form, Fit, Function, and Interface (F3I) DTR. Kihomac, Inc. is currently manufacturing the F3I DTR under contract SPRWA1-21-D-0015. The Government owns, or will provide under appropriate controls, the manufacturing and technical data necessary to support competitive production and repair of this item. The Government intends to compete this requirement on the open market to obtain new production units and repair services. The legacy B-52 DTR is repaired by Symetrics Industries (CAGE 22830) under contracts FA8539-20-D-0013 and FA8539-25-D-0004. This market research effort pertains to the F3I DTR identified above, currently being manufactured by Kihomac, Inc. under contract SPRWA1-21-D-0015, and is intended to identify sources capable of supporting competitive manufacture and repair using Government-owned technical data. The DTR is a Line Replaceable Unit (LRU) on the B-52 aircraft, with two DTRs installed per aircraft. The DTR transfers Offensive Avionics System (OAS) information to and from storage on the Data Transfer Cartridge (DTC) across its interface with the Fibre Channel or MIL-STD-1553A data bus system. Additionally, the DTR provides status over the MIL-STD-1553A and Fibre Channel buses indicating that the DTC is successfully installed. The required scope shall include, as applicable, manufacture and delivery of new production DTR units; hardware repair and return of unserviceable DTR units; obsolete parts resolution; engineering support to investigate Deficiency Reports (DRs); Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages (DMSMS) support; development, maintenance, and execution of required inspection, test, and acceptance procedures; and configuration management support to ensure newly manufactured and repaired units conform to the applicable Government-furnished technical data package. All newly manufactured and repaired units must meet applicable form, fit, function, and interface requirements. The contractor shall furnish all necessary material, support equipment, tools, test equipment, facilities, and services required to perform the work. The contractor is responsible for acquiring, maintaining, and calibrating all support equipment required at its primary or subcontractor facilities. Contractor-furnished material or replacement parts must equal or exceed the quality, tolerances, and specifications identified in the applicable technical data package. INSTRUCTIONS: 1. The document(s) below contain a description of the NSN listed for buy and repair requirements and a Contractor Capability Survey. Questions regarding this market survey should be addressed to Tyler Martens, Program Manager, 478-955-5165 or via email at tyler.martens.2@us.af.mil. DISCLAIMER: This Request for Information is for market research and planning purposes only. This is not a request for proposal, does not constitute a solicitation, and shall not be construed as a commitment by the government to award a contract. Responses to this RFI are not offers, and the Government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement.
